name: Rafael Rahman

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, parties or government. This is confidential. What is an ordinary shift like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 58 and run a drink-carton filler at a beverage plant. I have a vocational certificate and enough years at the filler to hear when the sealing jaw is out of rhythm. I check the first cartons, watch the fill level and ask the fitter before touching a guard. I like a line that runs clean without sticky cartons at the end.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is home like, and how do you use AI?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife coordinates meals at a hospital, and our grown children have moved away. We rent, my filler pay is about typical, and we have about three months of expenses saved. There are some other beverage and food plants nearby. I use AI every day to sketch recipes, organise messages and look up machine words, then check the answer with the fitter. I hope to stop at 68 in 2036 if documented income after work pays the bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the filler crew that a clever recipe app is not the same as a sealed drink carton. Someone must still watch the first pack after the jaw is changed. If software saves a little office time, fine; I want the line measured by leaks, not by slogans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Three months saved and my wife's regular hospital wage make the present rent manageable. I enjoy trying new tools, but a quiet AI future gives me no reason to change a safe filling routine for its own sake. We still need to work out whether 68 is affordable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep opening the first five cartons after each jaw change and record any leaking corner for the fitter. I'll add a small amount from each new pay packet to our reserve after rent. At home I'll keep using AI for everyday lists, but I won't treat an untested answer as a setting for the filler.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about today's work and bills. A sticky carton tells me more than a colourful forecast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does a weak carton seal look like?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A thin wet line appears where the corner should be sealed. I pull the carton, stop the run and ask the fitter to check the jaw pressure with its guard in place. If the first five pass, we let the rack move on.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make the reserve grow?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My wife's hospital meal hours are regular and we have roughly three months behind us. I would add from wages when the rent is paid, not shift the existing reserve between accounts. We can start the retirement budget without pretending the savings are income for life.

say: A **sealed drink carton** still needs a first-pack check.
Small office savings matter less than **actual leak rates** on the filler.
think: Three months saved and a **regular second wage** cover current rent.
I can enjoy new tools without changing a **safe filling routine** unnecessarily.
do: **Check** first cartons and record leaks for the fitter.
**Save** new wages after rent while keeping ordinary AI use separate from machine settings.
feel: **Calm** about present work and household money.
S0.quote: A sticky carton tells me more than a colourful forecast.
fieldNote: His **vocational experience** and typical pay combine with three months saved and a regular partner wage.
The **fresh reserve deposits** come from current wages; everyday AI use does not amount to new factory AI learning.

steps.text: Keep checking first five drink cartons after jaw changes
Save new filler wages after monthly rent

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say AI could plan orders and spot unusual fill readings before robots handle cartons. I would try an approved fault screen early if the fitter can check it beside the real pack. I would rather catch one leaking corner than stare at a perfect dashboard.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The screen could shorten checks or combine runs, and that might cut my paid changeover time. Three months saved gives us some room, but I would need wages beyond that. My daily home AI use makes me curious, not qualified to change a sealing jaw.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll ask the supervisor for permission to learn the plant's tested AI fault screen on paid time. With the fitter beside me, I'll compare its warning to actual cartons and learn the stop controls. I'll put the posted changeover rota beside four pay slips; if a funded paid guarded seal-check place opens, I'll enrol for the practical qualification.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about a possible cut to paid changeovers, though I can learn quickly. A dashboard cannot make a lost shift appear on a pay slip.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you learn on the fault screen?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The fitter can feed a known leaking carton through the inspection station and show me which alert corresponds to the wet seam. I would practise the screen's stop control with the machine guarded. A recipe prompt at home has never taught me that.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which number shows a real hour cut?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare paid changeover hours on the posted rota with four recent pay slips. If the number drops, I ask how the new schedule was set. I would not count a promised busy quarter as a paid hour yet.

say: **Order AI** may change planning before robots handle cartons.
A tested **fault screen** should be checked against real leaking packs.
think: Combined runs could reduce **paid changeover hours** and make our three-month reserve less comfortable.
Daily home AI use does not teach **guarded filler controls** or make me qualified to change a hot sealing jaw.
do: **Learn** the approved tested fault screen with the fitter on paid time.
**Compare** posted changeover hours with pay slips and enrol in funded guarded seal practice if offered.
feel: **Anxious** about possible own-hour cuts despite confidence learning tools.
S1.quote: A dashboard cannot make a lost shift appear on a pay slip.
fieldNote: His **adaptive use** includes new plant AI alert and stop controls, learned on approved paid time with the fitter.
The **seal-check qualification** requires an offered funded paid guarded practical place, separate from the fault-screen lesson.

steps.text: Learn approved tested AI fault controls with fitter on paid shift
Compare posted changeover rota with four pay slips
Enrol in seal checking if funded paid guarded place offered

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the crew thinking AI could plan drinks by 2028 and robots might fill and pack cartons around 2031, when I am 63. That is five years before I hope to stop. I want real paid-work plans and an early chance to learn the checks that remain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the filler rota to lose a lot of hours if robots can run the line. Our three-month reserve and some nearby plants give us a path, but my wife's hospital wage would not comfortably pay everything alone. I cannot turn 63 into retirement without actual income figures.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll ask the plant for written staffing hours and an offered funded paid guarded place in seal inspection. If that place opens, I'll enrol and complete the practical check. If filler hours fall, I'll apply to posted safe local food-packing roles only if net pay after travel covers rent; after qualifying, I'll apply to posted seal-inspection roles on the same terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about losing a large part of the rota, but I have options to work through. A training place is useful only when someone opens the door and pays the hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would seal-inspection training test?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I need to find a weak corner, trace the carton to its batch and stop the guarded test machine. The fitter should watch the practical run on paid time, with fees covered. I would not spend the household reserve on a company-required course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What makes a local posting worth taking?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The posting must name a local site, safe shifts and a base wage. We would subtract the journey and compare the rest with rent, food and my wife's actual hospital wage. The inspection role also needs the completed practical qualification.

say: **2031 robots** might run filler lines while I am 63.
The plant should offer **written staffing hours** and a real paid inspection place.
think: A large **filler-hour cut** could come before retirement is affordable.
Our **three-month reserve** and some nearby plants give choices, not lifelong income.
do: **Request** written hours and attend funded paid guarded inspection if offered.
**Apply** to posted safe local packing or qualified inspection if hours fall and net pay covers rent.
feel: **Anxious** about a large possible wage loss, with some alternatives.
S2.quote: A training place is useful only when someone opens the door and pays the hours.
fieldNote: He expects **large possible hour cuts** but can search nearby plants and use a three-month reserve to choose.
The **inspection job path** requires an actual funded paid guarded place, qualification and posted safe local work at viable net pay.

steps.text: Enrol in seal inspection if funded paid guarded place offered
Apply to posted safe local packing if hours fall and net pay covers rent
Apply to posted safe local inspection if qualified, hours fall, net pay covers rent

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say thinking AI might plan orders by 2031 and robots able to handle cartons could reach the filler around 2034, when I am 66. That gives me a little more time than the fast version. I still need paid years until the household numbers say we can stop.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The three-month reserve will not fund two years without wages. If we can afford to stop at 68 in 2036, good; if not, I will need a viable job when robots reach the filler. I can learn inspection early, but only a paid role brings money home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My wife and I will get written figures for income after I stop and put them beside rent and food. If those figures cover bills at 68, I'll leave the filler in 2036. If filler hours fall in 2034 while I still need wages, I'll enrol in an offered funded paid guarded seal-inspection course, then apply to a posted safe local inspection role after qualifying only if net pay after travel covers our costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the gap between the robot date and an affordable exit. Two years of rent is more than three months saved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What figures decide whether 2036 is affordable?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We need an actual monthly amount available when my wage stops, not a guess about a benefit. We will compare that with rent, food and other costs. If the figures fall short, I keep earning while safe work exists.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make inspection work real?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The course should include a supervised leak test on a guarded line with paid hours and covered fees. After passing, I would need a real local inspection posting whose base wage works after the bus fare. I won't call the course an offer of a job.

say: **2031 order AI** comes before filler robots around 2034.
I need **paid years** until documented income makes an exit possible.
think: Our **three-month reserve** cannot cover two years without work.
A **paid inspection role** would matter if I cannot afford to stop at 68.
do: **Compare** documented income and leave the filler in 2036 only if bills are covered.
**Train** if a funded paid guarded inspection place opens, then apply to posted safe local work if qualified and hours fall.
feel: **Anxious** about a possible wage gap before retirement.
S3.quote: Two years of rent is more than three months saved.
fieldNote: His **2036 stop** is conditional on actual post-work income, not an assumed benefit or automatic age.
The **inspection path** needs lost hours, funded paid guarded training, qualification and a posted safe local role at viable net pay.

steps.text: Compare documented post-work income with rent and food
Stop filler shift at 68 in 2036 if documented income covers bills
Enrol in inspection if funded paid guarded practical place offered
Apply to posted safe local inspection if qualified, hours fall, net pay sufficient

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say thinking AI might plan drinks in 2036, when I am 68, and robots could run the filler around 2039, when I am 71. I hope to have stopped at 68 if we can afford it. The long warning lets me check income and keep the line safe meanwhile.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Three months saved and my wife's regular hospital wage give us breathing space, not proof that I can stop. If documented income after work covers bills in 2036, I can leave before physical robots reach the filler. If it does not, I may need factory wages after 2036.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year my wife and I will compare written post-work income with rent, food and other costs. I'll keep the paid filler shift while we check. If the numbers cover bills, I'll stop in 2036 at 68; if I am still employed after 2036 and hours fall, I'll apply to posted safe local food-plant roles only when net pay after travel covers our costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy until the sums are confirmed, but ten years is time to get them. A filled carton today does not pay my rent forever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What figures would let you stop in 2036?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We need the monthly amount that would actually arrive after my wage ends. We will set it beside the same rent and food we pay now. If the sum fails, I won't hand in notice because a birthday came round.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When would you seek later food-plant work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would check the posted site, safe shift, paid hours and base wage. Travel comes off before I compare it with bills. I would send an application only if I was still working and my filler hours had fallen after 2036.

say: **2036 planning AI** precedes filler robots around 2039.
Stopping at **68** depends on documented income covering household costs.
think: Three months saved is **not permanent income**.
If verified income falls short, I may still need **paid work after 2036**.
do: **Compare** documented post-work income and stop the filler at 68 only if affordable.
**Keep** earning meanwhile; apply later only if still employed, hours fall and safe local net pay suffices.
feel: **Uneasy** about unverified retirement income with time to check it.
S4.quote: A filled carton today does not pay my rent forever.
fieldNote: His **2036 exit** follows a documented affordability decision rather than a presumed pension or automatic stop.
Any **post-2036 application** requires continued employment, lost hours and a real safe local food-plant role with adequate net pay.

steps.text: Compare documented post-work income with household rent and food
Keep paid drink-filler shifts while checking income figures
Stop filler shift at 68 in 2036 if documented income covers bills
Apply to posted safe local food if employed after 2036, hours fall, net pay sufficient

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: The fast 2028 case. Robots might take many filler hours at 63, five years before I hope to stop. Written paid shifts, funded paid guarded inspection and real safe local jobs with enough net pay would help. I need actual household income figures before choosing 2036.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who opens the first carton after a sealing jaw is changed. A dry conveyor can still carry a leaking drink carton.

headlineQuote: A dry conveyor can still carry a leaking drink carton.
portrait: **Rafael**, 58, is an experienced drink-carton filler operator with a vocational certificate and daily checked AI use.
He and his hospital-meals-coordinator wife have **grown children**, typical pay, three months saved and some nearby food plants.
His **centrist outlook** follows measured results; his adaptive habits make him eager to learn approved AI controls with the fitter.
He is **anxious** about fast filler-hour loss; stopping at 68 depends on documented household income covering bills.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could bring filler robots by 2031 and cut paid hours at 63.
whatWouldHelp: **Written paid shifts**, funded paid guarded inspection and real safe local jobs with enough net pay would help.
